summary: The scheduler slice is largely implemented: scoring covers class bias, explicit priority, bounded age/fairness, retry and human boosts; score summaries are persisted and exposed; ordered/deferred records are written; owned-path overlap remains advisory; and the focused, full unit, lint, type, and coverage validations pass. One scheduler selection gap remains against the plan's SKIP LOCKED/concurrency requirement.
gaps: Fix WorkspaceRepository.list_schedulable_ids/_schedulable_workspace_ids_stmt so Postgres polling applies a bounded candidate LIMIT/window with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. The current helper deletes the limit and selects all matching Workspace rows before Python-side score sorting, so a worker can lock/fetch the whole schedulable queue instead of a bounded candidate set.

Add a regression for the Postgres scheduler query/selection shape that fails on an unbounded FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED scan and proves the selected candidate window is bounded while still allowing Python-side score ordering and suppressed-row refill behavior.
